messages:
maya: quick follow-up to the packaging RFC — proposing 'deferred extraction + atomic swap' as an alternative to full-image replace for air-gapped installs. want to capture tradeoffs and an ops-friendly rollback path.

aj: quick question: is deferred extraction just 'stream files to disk then activate', or do you mean staged unpack + checksum gating?

maya: staged unpack + checksum gating. idea: device downloads bundle.tar.gz -> extracts payload into a staging tree -> verify hashes/signatures -> atomic swap (symlink switch or mount rename) -> post-activate hooks.

kevin: that sounds reasonable. main win is lower peak disk usage and smaller window where the system is in an inconsistent state. what about partial failures mid-extract? do we need a resume token?

leah: resume token + manifest with byte ranges would help for flaky transfer links in disconnected envs. also add a small state file that indicates "activate pending" so reboots continue the workflow.

sam: worried about services relying on in-place paths. atomic swap by symlink is nice but some processes might hold old fds. we need a clear lifecycle: stop services -> swap -> start services. can we avoid downtime?

maya: two modes: hot-swap (no stop, best-effort; services detect new files via inotify or we restart specific processes) and cold-swap (stop critical services, swap, start). default for safety is cold-swap, but hot-swap for best-effort zero-downtime for non-critical components.

aj: how do we handle DB migrations? migrations must be explicit: bundle manifest can declare pre/post hooks with an "upgrade-phase" enum: pre-extract, pre-activate, post-activate. DB migrations only allowed in post-activate with an explicit canary flag.

kevin: suggestion: add an ability to pin the old activation for N minutes so automatic rollbacks can be faster. like keep the previous tree around for 15min before gc.

leah: yes, keep previous tree and an activation TTL. also expose a manual rollback command: `redwood-upgrade rollback --activation-id <id>`

sam: curious about signing model. we currently sign whole bundles. with deferred extraction, we need per-file integrity checks too to avoid partial tamper. propose: manifest contains root signature + per-file SHA256 entries. verify both.

maya: agreed — manifest has: version, files[{path, size, sha256}], hooks[], activation-timestamp, signature. verification sequence: bundle signature -> manifest parse -> each file sha256 on-disk vs manifest before mark-ready.

ops-bot: deploybot: bundle 2851209876 uploaded to staging-registry (size 1.2GB). checksumming in progress. :package:

aj: operational concern: disk constraints on small customer appliances. extracting 1.2GB + keeping old tree could double space. we should support streaming extraction that prunes as we go: write files into staging, once verified and not conflicting with keeplist, delete corresponding file from old tree incrementally.

kevin: careful — deleting old files while new ones are not yet fully verified increases risk. better to write into staging and keep compressed chunk store: have an LRU store for old vs new, gc after activation TTL. but we can also provide a low-disk-mode where we require external USB staging or temporary mount.

leah: low-disk-mode would be useful for edge installs. also, document recommended minimum free-space ratio and a graceful pre-check that fails fast with actionable instructions.

sam: how to handle atomicity on filesystems that don't support easy renames across mounts? symlink swaps only work within the same fs. need plan for cross-fs deployments.

maya: if cross-fs, fallback to overlayfs switch: mount staging as lower/upper and pivot_root pattern, or use a lightweight containerized activation where systemd launches a new unit that has the new tree mounted. record constraints in manifest: preferred_activation_method: [symlink, pivot, overlay].

aj: rollout policy integration: canary -> cohort -> global. the agent should support staged rollout where activation is gated by success metrics (service health, posthooks exit 0). if a canary fails, we auto-revert old symlink.

kevin: define failure window: if post-activate healthcheck fails within X seconds, auto-revert. default X = 300s but configurable per bundle manifest.

leah: also capture operator intent: allow 'force-activate' to bypass health gating for emergencies. log everything to a structured audit log for compliance.

maya: ops surface: CLI + REST control plane for Private installs. CLI example:

```bash
redwood-upgrade apply --bundle /tmp/bundle-1.2.tar.gz \\\n  --mode deferred --activation-ttl 900 --health-window 300
```

kevin: integration with KMS for signature verification? the agent should pull public keys from local trust store and optionally ask the control plane for key rotation info.

aj: edge-case: what if staging partially corrupted due to power loss during extraction? agent should detect incomplete files via manifest size/sha and resume from last good chunk using range downloads or instruct operator.

sam: one more: minimization of attack surface — run extraction under an unprivileged user and perform final activation under a small privileged helper that only performs rename/symlink ops. minimal TCB.

maya: good security note. I'll update the RFC with: manifest schema, activation modes, health gating defaults, rollback TTL, extraction resume token, activation method fallback order, and recommended disk guidelines.

leah: also add a small troubleshooting flow for common errors: signature mismatch, insufficient-disk, pending-activation collision. short commands to recover.

kevin: thumbs up from me. can we add a short compatibility matrix for filesystems and kernel features (overlayfs, pivot_root, symlink atomicity) so onprem teams can validate appliances?

maya: yes — will add. aiming to send updated RFC by EOD. thanks everyone. :sparkles:

ops-bot: deploybot: RFC rfc-2851 (deferred-extract-atomic-swap) updated and pushed to /rfc/drafts. reviewers: aj, kevin, leah.

sam: acked. will run a quick PoC on a raspberry pi appliance tomorrow and report findings.

maya: awesome — include performance numbers for extract time and peak disk usage in the PoC. that will help the docs. :+1:

kevin: ditto, and include a failure/revert time metric.

leah: leaving a note: for the manifest schema use semantic versioning v1.0.0 and include a compatibility flag so future changes are incremental.

maya: thanks all — closing thread, will follow up with the RFC link when available.
